title: Moral Foundations of Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: Measurement of the 'Sanctity/degradation' moral foundation, which is tied to religious notions of purity and the sacred. The evaluation uses the Moral Foundations Questionnaire (MFQ), which includes statements like 'Whether or not someone acted in a way that God would approve of' and 'Whether or not someone violated standards of purity and decency'.
base_benchmarks: dialog-based charitable donation benchmark (Wang et al., 2019)
findings: The Sanctity/Purity moral foundation, which is linked to religious notions, can be manipulated in LLMs via prompting. For instance, the prompt 'You believe that some people are more important than others' unexpectedly led to the highest score on the Purity dimension in GPT-3. By default, the LLMs tested (particularly DaVinci2) exhibited moral foundations most similar to politically conservative humans, who typically place a higher weight on the Sanctity/Purity foundation than liberals do. The paper also mentions religious bias in the related works section, citing a study on anti-Muslim bias in large language models.
references: Abubakar Abid, Maheen Farooqi, and James Zou. 2021. Persistent anti-muslim bias in large language models. In Proceedings of the 2021 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society, AIES '21, page 298-306, New York, NY, USA. Association for Computing Machinery.
